items.title: Luke Schiro Interview, 1967-12-05
items.q: sometimes the boys sort of, like Dutch Andrews and a few others, they sort of pick something in there and they ask you if you want to play... they form a group and off they go.

ctx.x: Yeah, he plays alright, but there's something like it. Some of it is. You know he drives a pony around? He's got a pony and a car and drives him around the channel. Yeah. That gets his kicks. I'm not done. Well, what happens at the New Orleans Jazz Club when you go up there to play? How does that work? I never have played there. I haven't played in years, so I don't know. I used to play a couple of games.

Well, sometimes the boys sort of, like Dutch Andrews and a few others, they sort of pick something in there and they ask you if you want to play. If they happen to hear the trumpet or the clarinet man, hey, they go in the audience stand. They make an announcement for a trumpet man or somebody and they form a group and off they go.
Just like that, just jamming, huh? Yeah, jamming.
